| 🪢 Tangle · [q-0037.0013.0006](docs/questions/q-0037.0013.0006-how-is-the-path-ahead-found-and-shown-the-space-of-open-questions-and-tickets-mapped-from-the-roots-the-next-slices-ranked-by-a-stated-criterion-and-the-picture.md) · [q-0037.0012.0009](docs/questions/q-0037.0012.0009-how-is-an-amendment-to-an-instruction-tested-before-it-lands-against-which-cases-chosen-how-run-with-no-instruction-the-standing-one-and-the-new-one.md) · — · — |
|---|

| 📍 **q-0037.0013.0006** · How is the path ahead found and shown: the space of open questions and tickets mapped from the roots, the next slices ranked by a stated criterion, and the picture the person sees? |
|---|

Because the queue is made of tickets and the rule speaks of slices, and I followed both without asking what the space is. A ticket is a question whose `Where it stands` was accepted: the trodden part. The map is the store, and you had said so, *tied to the question roots*. The tree read from its roots is now in the question's body; the short of it:

| root | open | with a ticket |
|---|---|---|
| what the project is for | 5 | 0 |
| how it is built | 158 | 74 |
| the landscape it evolves in | 2 | 0 |

What this view shows that the ticket view could not:

- **The work stands almost wholly under one root.** The purpose root and the landscape root hold seven open questions between them and not one ticket. The compounding criterion is a criterion for *how it is built*; it is blind to the other two by construction. And [q-0038.0001](docs/questions/q-0038.0001-does-working-under-the-harness-deliver-software-better-than-working-without-it-measured-on-the-same-work.md), whether working under the harness delivers better, measured, is the question whose answer says if the compounding is worth anything at all.
- **Inside the built root, the criterion sorts the subtrees, not the tickets.** Meta-rules first, with q-0037.0012.0009 aligning; then rules reaching their occasion, [q-0037.0011](docs/questions/q-0037.0011-does-each-rule-reach-the-occasion-it-is-for.md), struck four times; then this question's own parent, the next step; then the tests; then the store, seventeen open and three ticketed. Recipients, where thirty-four of the seventy-four tickets sit, hand the harness's own development the least.
- **The strike count is a column tickets lack.** The reply's form, [q-0037.0016](docs/questions/q-0037.0016-how-does-a-reply-show-the-principles-each-of-its-claims-stands-on-and-where-are-the-principles-named-for-it.md), struck eight times, is where sessions keep returning without closing. That is a cost the path should show.
- **A subtree opened wide and left.** Twenty-one open under *does each skill state only what it owns*, two with a ticket. Whether to prune it or to mint from it is exactly a pathfinder's question, and no ticket view would have raised it.

So the shape sharpens: the pathfinder reads the store from the roots, weighs each subtree by what its answer would hand the next one, by its strikes, and by how much of it is already minted, and draws the path over that; tickets are what the path has reached, not what it ranks. The ordering criterion then needs a second clause the ticket reading hid: how the three roots weigh against each other, since no criterion inside one root can see the others. That is above the dial, 🛠️ development=a product slice, and yours (💡 [*Above it, it settles nothing*](AGENTS.md:221)).

| ⚖️ Decisions |
|---|
| How the three roots weigh against each other in the path, which the compounding criterion cannot say |
| The pathfinder's shape: the pacer's first slice under [01-0020](docs/tickets/01-0020-each-turn-knows-its-next-step.md), or a skill of its own |
| The rewording to *develop itself better*, landing in the queue on your yes |
| [q-0037.0012.0003](docs/questions/q-0037.0012.0003-what-does-an-entry-contract-version-cover.md) waits at `/align`, as the queue has held since 2026-10-08 |
